map.Lessons 6-13, 6-7 & 6-12 — break numbers: Lessons 6-13, 6-7 & 6-12. Break numbers into prime gears. Mesh them with the greatest common factor. Time them with the least common multiple. Four gates stand in the way. The engine is stuck. The city needs it to run.
map.Previously: Axiom City runs on the Patte: Before: Axiom City runs on the Pattern Engine. It is a tall stack of gears. It turns on whole-number rules. Tonight, gear 12 and gear 18 stopped. They do not fit. The city lights blink.
map.Previously: the team mapped every street: Before: the team mapped Axiom City. Each street is on the Engine's number grid. Now the main gears are stuck. The math built them. Only that math can start them again.
map.The core gears jammed — twelve teeth gri: The main gears are stuck. Twelve teeth grind on eighteen. I'm the keeper tonight. We must know what these gears are MADE of. Until then, nothing turns.
map.Made of? Just hit the override and FORCE: Made of? Just pull the big lever. FORCE it, kid! Who has time to take it apart?
map.Force snaps teeth. We do it right: every: Force snaps teeth. We do it right. Each gear breaks down into prime parts. They are the tiny bits of the Engine. Find them. Then the gears show us how to fit.
map.The Factor Forge — where the keepers spl: The Factor Forge. Here the keepers split a number into its primes.
map.Watch: 36 splits into 4 and 9. Neither i: Watch: 36 splits into 4 and 9. Each one is not prime. So I keep going. 4 = 2×2, 9 = 3×3. The blue-green rings are the primes.
map.Definitions, keepers: a prime number has: Words, keepers: a prime number has two factors, no more. They are 1 and the number (2, 3, 5, 7, 11…). A factor tree keeps splitting. It stops when each branch ends on a prime. Those primes are the prime factorization.
map.To find a number's prime factorization,: To find a prime factorization, make a factor tree. Split into two factors. Split the ones that are not prime. Stop when each branch is a prime number. So 36 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3.
map.Your turn, reader — two gears, two trees: Your turn, reader. Two gears. Two trees. Take each one all the way down to primes.
map.The Engine only accepts PRIME gears. Bre: The Engine takes only PRIME gears. Break each number all the way down. Pick one factor tree. All its ends are prime numbers.
map.Conceptual: a prime number has exactly t: Conceptual: a prime number has two factors, no more. They are 1 and the number (2, 3, 5, 7, 11…). Keep splitting until each branch ends on a prime.
map.Procedural: split off a factor, then spl: Procedural: split off a factor. Then split each part that is not prime. 36 → 4 × 9 → (2×2) × (3×3). Stop when every factor is prime.
map.Gear 24 and gear 36 only mesh on teeth t: Gear 24 and gear 36 fit only on teeth they SHARE. Too big a gear won't fit. Too small wastes power. We need the GREATEST one that fits both.
map.…and the biggest shared one is the great: …and the top one is the greatest common factor.
map.A factor divides a number evenly. The gr: A factor divides a number evenly. The greatest common factor (GCF) is the biggest factor. Both numbers share it. Fast way: factor both into primes. Multiply the primes they share. 24 & 36 share 2×2×3 = 12.
map.Reader — find the greatest gear that mes: Reader, find the greatest gear that fits each pair. The Mesh Lock wants that one. Not less.
map.Two gears mesh only on the teeth they SH: Two gears fit only on the teeth they SHARE. Find the greatest common factor. It is the top gear that fits both. GCF(24, 36) and GCF(18, 30).
map.Conceptual: the GCF is the largest numbe: Conceptual: the GCF divides into BOTH. It is the top number that does. It is never more than the smaller number.
map.Procedural: factor each, then multiply t: Procedural: factor each. Then multiply the primes they share. 24 = 2×2×2×3 and 36 = 2×2×3×3 share 2×2×3 = 12. 18 = 2×3×3 and 30 = 2×3×5 share 2×3 = 6.
map.The timing ring. Two gears start tooth-t: The timing ring. Two gears start tooth to tooth. Then they spin. The Engine won't start until they line up again.
map.Gear 6 and gear 8 click back to their st: Gear 6 and gear 8 click back to the start. That needs a whole number of turns on BOTH. How many teeth until they line up?
map.A multiple is what you get counting by a: Count by a number to get a multiple: 6, 12, 18, 24… — The least common multiple? It is the first number in BOTH lists. It is never less than the bigger gear.
map.A multiple of a number is that number ti: A multiple of a number is that number times 1, 2, 3… — The least common multiple (LCM)? It is the smallest multiple both share. Fast way: factor both. Take each prime the most times it appears. 6 & 8 → 2×2×2×3 = 24.
map.Run the rings, reader — find the fewest: Run the rings, reader. Find the fewest teeth. When does each pair line up again?
map.Two gears start aligned, then spin. They: Two gears start lined up. Then they spin. They line up again at their least common multiple. LCM(6, 8) and LCM(4, 10). How many teeth until each pair lines up?
map.Conceptual: a common multiple sits in BO: Conceptual: a common multiple is in BOTH counting lists. The LEAST common multiple is the smallest one. It is never less than the bigger number.
map.Procedural: factor each, then take every: Procedural: factor each. Then take each prime the MOST times it appears. 6 = 2×3 and 8 = 2×2×2 → 2×2×2×3 = 24. 4 = 2×2 and 10 = 2×5 → 2×2×5 = 20.
map.Late shift. The core gears are nearly re: It is late. The main gears are almost set. Then Bram finds the big lever.
map.Twelve times eighteen — TWO HUNDRED SIXT: Twelve times eighteen. That is TWO HUNDRED SIXTEEN turns. Then they line up! I'll spin it that far. I'll FORCE the start!
map.216 is WAY too far — you'll grind the te: 216 is WAY too far. The teeth will grind to dust first. These gears share parts. They line up much sooner.
map.Distortion spike. 12 × 18 is A common mu: Big glitch. 12 × 18 is A common multiple. It is not the LEAST. The gears share a factor. If you skip it, you go too far. Find the real one. Do it before he breaks the Engine.
map.Three locks to restart: the greatest gea: Three locks to start it again. The greatest gear that fits them. The fewest teeth until they line up. And just what Bram got wrong.
map.The gears are honest. The override isn't: The gears tell the truth. The lever does not. Reader, take the boss.
Boss Gate: the main gears are 12 and 18. Find their GCF and LCM. Then name the flaw in Bram's "216 turns."
map.BOSS GATE. Three locks. Mesh the gears,: BOSS GATE. Three locks. Fit the gears. Time the gears. Show the lever lie.
map.The master gears have 12 teeth and 18 te: The two big gears have 12 teeth and 18 teeth. Set both dials to start the Engine. Bram is pulling the big lever now! Three locks:
map.Fewest teeth until they realign: LCM(12,: Fewest teeth until they line up: LCM(12, 18) =
map.Bram yells \"the gears realign after 12: Bram yells: "the gears line up after 12 × 18 = 216 turns!" What is wrong?
map.Conceptual: the GCF is the largest gear: Conceptual: GCF: the top gear that fits both (≤ the smaller). LCM: the fewest teeth until they line up (≥ the larger).
map.Gear 6 meshes them, realign at 36 — and: Gear 6 fits them. They line up at 36. The Engine starts on the FIRST try. No force. The city lights are back. They are bright and steady.
map.Thirty-six?! Not… two hundred sixteen? F: Thirty-six?! Not… two hundred sixteen? Fine. Next time I'll read the gears first. Then I'll pull a lever.
map.The Engine runs on whole gears — but the: The Engine runs on whole gears. But the city pays in decimals. To be continued…
map.Break it down.Every whole number is buil: Break it down.Each whole number is built from primes. A factor tree splits it. Each branch ends in a prime. 36 = 2×2×3×3.
map.Mesh it.The greatest common factor is th: Mesh it.The greatest common factor: the top gear both share. Multiply the primes they share. GCF(24, 36) = 12.
map.Time it.The least common multiple is the: Time it.The least common multiple is the first shared multiple. Take each prime the most times it appears. LCM(6, 8) = 24. It is never less than the bigger number.
map.The override trap.GCF is small (it fits: The override trap.GCF is small (it fits inside both). LCM is big (both fit inside it). Bram did 12×18 = 216. He skipped the factor of 6 the gears share. They really line up at 36.
map.\"A number you can't take apart, you don: "Can't take a number apart? Then you don't know it. Find its primes. Then the machine is not a puzzle." — A.V.
map.completed Unit 1 · Episode 3: The Patter: completed Unit 1 · Episode 3: The Pattern Engine. They know prime factorization. And greatest common factor. And least common multiple.
map.Next up — U1·E4: Exact Change — is warmi: Next up: U1·E4: Exact Change. It is warming up in the Engine's money room.
map.Different number: build the factor tree: A new number: build the factor tree for 18.
map.18 splits into 2 × 9. The 2 is prime — c: 18 splits into 2 × 9. The 2 is prime. Circle it. 9 is not prime. So split again: 9 = 3 × 3.
map.Bottom of the tree: 18 = 2 × 3 × 3 — all: The tree ends: 18 = 2 × 3 × 3. All are primes. Read the circled numbers.
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
A new pair: the GCF of 8 and 12.
Prime factors: 8 = 2×2×2 and 12 = 2×2×3. Circle what they SHARE: two 2's.
A new pair: the LCM of 4 and 6.
map.4 = 2×2 and 6 = 2×3. Take each prime the: 4 = 2×2 and 6 = 2×3. Take each prime the most times it shows up: 2×2 (from 4) and 3 (from 6).
map.Multiply: 2 × 2 × 3 = 12. LCM(4, 6) = 12: Multiply: 2 × 2 × 3 = 12. LCM(4, 6) = 12. And 12 is in both lists (4, 8, 12 / 6, 12).
map.Check: GCF × LCM = 4 × 40 = 160, and 8 ×: Check: GCF × LCM = 4 × 40 = 160. And 8 × 20 = 160. The two always multiply back to the product.
map.Two numbers have a GCF of 3 and a produc: Two numbers have a GCF of 3. Their product is 90. What is their LCM?
Pick one tree for EACH gear. Then check.
map.4 × 9 does multiply to 36, but 4 and 9 a: 4 × 9 does multiply to 36. But 4 and 9 are NOT prime. Your tree stopped too soon. Split 4 = 2×2 and 9 = 3×3.
map.6 is not prime — it still splits into 2: 6 is not prime. It still splits into 2 × 3. Keep going until each branch is prime.
map.9 is not prime — split it into 3 × 3. A: 9 is not prime. Split it into 3 × 3. A prime tree ends with no composite numbers.
map.4 × 15 equals 60, but neither 4 nor 15 i: 4 × 15 is 60. But 4 is not prime. 15 is not prime. Split both: 4 = 2×2 and 15 = 3×5.
map.30 is not prime — that's just the first: 30 is not prime. That is just the first split. Keep going: 30 = 2×3×5.
map.10 is not prime — split it into 2 × 5. E: 10 is not prime. Split it into 2 × 5. Each factor at the end must be prime.
map.36 = 2×2×3×3 and 60 = 2×2×3×5 — pure pri: 36 = 2×2×3×3 and 60 = 2×2×3×5. All prime gears. The Forge takes them.
12 fits 24 and 36. 6 fits 18 and 30. The top shared gears lock in.
map.72 is the LEAST COMMON MULTIPLE of 24 an: 72 is the LEAST COMMON MULTIPLE of 24 and 36. It is the smallest number they both divide into. The GCF divides into BOTH. It is the top number that does. So it must be ≤ 24.
map.6 divides both 24 and 36, but it isn't t: 6 divides both 24 and 36. But it is not the GREATEST. 12 does too. Multiply ALL the shared primes (2×2×3), not just some.
map.4 divides 24 and 36, but you missed the: 4 divides 24 and 36. But you missed the shared 3. The shared primes are 2×2×3 = 12.
map.90 is the LEAST COMMON MULTIPLE of 18 an: 90 is the LEAST COMMON MULTIPLE of 18 and 30. It is not the GCF. The greatest common factor is less than both numbers.
map.That divides both, but it isn't the grea: That divides both. But it is not the greatest. 18 and 30 share 2 AND 3. Multiply them: 2×3 = 6.
map.First box: list the primes 24 and 36 sha: First box: list the primes 24 and 36 share. Multiply them: 2×2×3.
map.24 teeth and 20 teeth — the gears click: 24 teeth and 20 teeth. The gears click back in place. They are in time.
map.48 is just 6 × 8. That's a common multip: 48 is just 6 × 8. That is a common multiple. But it is not the LEAST. The gears share a factor of 2. So divide it out: 48 ÷ 2 = 24.
map.2 is the GREATEST COMMON FACTOR of 6 and: 2 is the GREATEST COMMON FACTOR of 6 and 8. It is not the LCM. The least common multiple: the smallest number BOTH divide into. So it must be ≥ 8.
map.6 divides 12, but 8 does not. The LCM mu: 6 divides 12, but 8 does not. The LCM must be in BOTH lists. Keep going to 24.
map.40 is just 4 × 10. They share a factor o: 40 is just 4 × 10. They share a factor of 2. Divide it out: 40 ÷ 2 = 20.
map.2 is the GREATEST COMMON FACTOR of 4 and: 2 is the GREATEST COMMON FACTOR of 4 and 10. It is not the LCM. The LCM must be ≥ 10.
map.First pair: take 2 the most times it app: First pair: take 2 the most times it appears (three times, from 8). Times 3 → 24.
map.Lock 1 wants the GREATEST COMMON FACTOR,: Lock 1 wants the GREATEST COMMON FACTOR. But 36 is the LCM. You mixed them up. The GCF is the top gear that fits BOTH. So it is ≤ 12.
map.Lock 1 holds. 12 = 2×2×3 and 18 = 2×3×3: Lock 1 holds. 12 = 2×2×3 and 18 = 2×3×3 share 2×3. Multiply the shared primes.
map.Lock 2 wants the LEAST COMMON MULTIPLE,: Lock 2 wants the LEAST COMMON MULTIPLE. But 6 is the GCF. Mixed up again. The LCM: the fewest teeth until they line up. So it is ≥ 18.
map.Lock 2 holds, but 216 = 12 × 18 isn't th: Lock 2 holds. 216 = 12 × 18 is not the LEAST. Divide out the shared factor 6: 216 ÷ 6 = 36.
map.Lock 3 holds. Multiplying isn't the slip: Lock 3 holds. Multiplying is not the slip on its own. The problem is the NUMBER he gets. Compare 216 to the real LCM.
map.Lock 3 holds. Realignment really is abou: Lock 3 holds. Lining up is about a MULTIPLE, not the GCF. But his multiple is too big. Why?
map.Lock 3 holds. The gears share a factor o: Lock 3 holds. The gears share a factor of 6. So they line up at 36, not 216. Pick what went wrong.
map.ALL LOCKS OPEN. GCF 6, LCM 36 — and Bram: ALL LOCKS OPEN. GCF 6, LCM 36. Bram's 216 skipped the factor of 6 the gears share. The Pattern Engine roars back to life.
Yes! Now go back and open that gate.
